Revised assessment: The statement acknowledges a sharp near-term drag from COVID-19, but the FOMC’s swift move to the effective lower bound, “at least” $700B in Treasury/MBS purchases, expanded repos, discount-window easing, reserve-requirement changes, and coordinated dollar swap lines aligns with the literature on policy at the zero lower bound and the credit channel. Credit-view evidence (Bernanke–Gertler; Oliner and Rudebusch; Gertler and Gilchrist) indicates such measures reduce external finance premia and help sustain business fixed investment and household spending by stabilizing balance sheets. With market-based inflation compensation falling and expectations roughly anchored below 2 percent, inflation-forecast-targeting guidance (Svensson; Svensson and Woodford) supports aggressive easing to re-anchor expectations and avoid deflation risk. Overall tone remains negative on growth and the outlook, but the forceful, multi-tool response materially mitigates downside risks, warranting a moderately (not strongly) negative sentiment.
